page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and supports hyper-threading. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with the PassMark memory score placing in the top tier (top 10%) and large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths ranking in the top 25% at 247.43 GB/sec and 159.49 GB/sec respectively. Single-core CPU performance is also in the top 10% according to stress-ng testing, while multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores align with the middle 50% average. Single-threaded compression and decompression benchmarks show strong results in the top 25%, whereas multi-threaded decompression and database operations fall into the average category. LLM inference benchmarks show average performance for small 135M models, but prompt processing for medium 7B models drops to the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 makes this instance a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute scaling. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention. This profile is suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, caching layers such as Redis, and general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute cores.
